chunks: Humeed ibn Ziyad from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from one of his companions, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who died and left a slave boy, so one of the inheritors testified that he was free. He said: If the witness is reliable, his testimony is accepted for his share, and he is asked to work (or compensate) for what belongs to the other inheritors.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave's emancipation if one heir testifies he is free?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of partial emancipation (tadbir) in Shia jurisprudence, where a reliable heir's testimony validates the slave's freedom only for his proportional share of the estate. For the remaining shares belonging to other heirs, the slave must work or pay compensation, reflecting the practical application of inheritance law and the importance of witness credibility (riwāyah) in resolving financial disputes among co-heirs.
